hla.assumption: HLA type is assumed, not measured. The public tumour data carries no HLA typing, so these are illustrative panels of commonly observed class I alleles. Real neoantigen selection uses the patient's own sequenced HLA type, and a different HLA type would select different peptides from the identical tumour.

limitations: HLA type is assumed, not measured. The public tumour data carries none, and a different HLA type would select different peptides from the identical tumour.
No matched normal sample, so some variants here may be inherited rather than acquired by the tumour.
No variant phasing or clonality: mutations present in only part of the tumour are treated the same as those in every cell.
No immunogenicity model. Being presented is not the same as provoking a useful T-cell response.
No self-proteome subtraction, and no manufacturing constraints.
